heroLead: Point Marion sits right on the Monongahela at the West Virginia border, the southernmost tip of Fayette County, where mineral ownership questions sometimes get complicated by exactly which side of a nearby line a parcel falls on.
intro: We've worked with families near Point Marion whose land straddles old surveys that predate modern GPS boundaries, which can make confirming exact acreage and county jurisdiction more involved than it would be elsewhere. That's not something to be intimidated by — it's just a step we take seriously before quoting a number.

sections.heading: Border-Area Title Confirmation
paragraphs: Before we make an offer on a Point Marion tract, we confirm the parcel is recorded in Fayette County, Pennsylvania, and pull the deed chain directly from the recorder of deeds office in Uniontown. If there's any ambiguity in the boundary description tied to the property's location near the state line, we sort that out as part of the review rather than leaving it for you to untangle later.

This part of Fayette County sits on the southern edge of wet-gas Marcellus activity, and development has been less dense here than further north in Washington and Greene counties, so we price honestly against what's actually happening in your specific area rather than a countywide average.

sections.heading: Family Land That's Crossed Generations
paragraphs: A lot of Point Marion mineral interests have passed through several generations of the same family without much attention paid to the paperwork, especially once a farm stopped being actively worked. We'll walk you through whatever estate or title cleanup is needed, in plain language, before a sale can close.

faqs.question: My property is close to the West Virginia line. Does that complicate a sale?
faqs.answer: We confirm your parcel is recorded in Fayette County, Pennsylvania as part of our review, which resolves most border-area questions before they become a problem.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling near Point Marion?
faqs.answer: Activity in this part of Fayette County is lighter than in core Washington or Greene County areas, and we'll tell you honestly what we find near your specific tract.

faqs.question: What if my family's ownership records are incomplete?
faqs.answer: We trace the recorded chain of title from the Fayette County courthouse and explain what steps, if any, are needed to clear it.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests on both sides of the Monongahela near town?
faqs.answer: Yes, our review covers any Fayette County parcel regardless of which side of the river it sits on, as long as the mineral rights are recorded in Pennsylvania.
